# The state contract

An agent declares what it is doing by writing a JSON document into its workspace directory. This page is the contract, rendered from the table the decoder types members against, so a member described here and a member the decoder accepts are the same member.

`agentfs schema` prints the contract as a JSON Schema 2020-12 document. Its `$id` is `https://stxkxs.github.io/agentfs/schema/agent-state.v1.json`, which the release workflow serves from `schema/` on a release tag — until one is pushed, the identifier names the document without resolving to it, and `agentfs schema` is where to fetch it. `agentfs validate <directory>` checks a workspace against the same rules.

## Where the document lives

Each immediate subdirectory of the workspace is one agent. The agent's state document is the first of these names it holds:

| Name | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `state.json` | canonical |
| `status.json` | accepted, with an info diagnostic naming `state.json` |
| `agent.json` | accepted, with an info diagnostic naming `state.json` |

A directory holding `logs`, `memory`, `artifacts`, `tools`, `runs` is recognized as an agent workspace even when it declares no state document, which is how an agent that writes only logs is seen.

## Members

A member the contract does not define is preserved and reported with an info diagnostic, so an integrator's own fields survive a round trip through agentfs without becoming contractual.

| Member | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `string` | yes | The contract version the document declares. |
| `status` | `string` | yes | The state the agent declares itself to be in. |
| `agent` | `string` | no | The agent's name. The workspace directory name is used when absent. |
| `task` | `string` | no | The work in progress. |
| `step` | `integer` or `string` | no | The position within the task: a non-negative ordinal or a named phase. |
| `steps_total` | `integer` | no | The number of steps the task is expected to take. |
| `model` | `string` | no | The model the agent is running against. |
| `run_id` | `string` | no | The run directory this document belongs to. |
| `problem` | `string` | no | A fault description, independent of status. |
| `heartbeat_seconds` | `number` | no | How often the agent undertakes to rewrite the document. A document older than this is reported stale. |
| `started_at` | `string` (date-time) | no | When the agent began the task, as an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset. |
| `updated_at` | `string` (date-time) | no | When the agent last wrote the document, as an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset. |
| `labels` | `object` | no | Integrator-defined string metadata. |

### Length ceilings

A state document is a status declaration rather than a log. A member longer than its ceiling is truncated for display and reported.

| Member | Ceiling |
| --- | --- |
| `agent` | 256 runes |
| `task` | 4096 runes |
| `model` | 256 runes |
| `run_id` | 256 runes |
| `problem` | 4096 runes |

### Compatibility member names

Read under the compatibility profile only, each with an info diagnostic naming the canonical member.

| Member | Also accepted as |
| --- | --- |
| `problem` | `error` |

## The status vocabulary

`status` is matched exactly against a closed set, after trimming and case folding. A value outside it raises a diagnostic naming the accepted set. Matching is never by substring, so `"not running"` is not running and `"unfailed"` is not a failure.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `running` | The agent holds work and is progressing. |
| `idle` | The agent holds no work and is available. |
| `blocked` | The agent holds work it cannot progress without an external input. |
| `error` | The agent stopped because it could not continue. |
| `done` | The agent completed its work. |

## Status and problem are independent

`problem` describes a fault. It does not set `status`, and `status` does not imply it. A reader that derived one from the other could not express either of these:

```json
{"schema": "agentfs/v1", "status": "done",    "problem": "The first pass timed out and was retried."}
{"schema": "agentfs/v1", "status": "running", "problem": "A transient 503; retrying."}
```

A `status` of `error` with no `problem` leaves a reader nothing to act on, and raises a warning.

## The compatibility profile

A document declaring no `schema` member is read under the compatibility profile: the spellings below resolve, each with an info diagnostic naming the canonical form. Under `agentfs/v1` only the vocabulary above is accepted.

| Spelling | Resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `active` | `running` |
| `awaiting_approval` | `blocked` |
| `awaiting_input` | `blocked` |
| `busy` | `running` |
| `complete` | `done` |
| `completed` | `done` |
| `crashed` | `error` |
| `failed` | `error` |
| `failure` | `error` |
| `fatal` | `error` |
| `finished` | `done` |
| `in-progress` | `running` |
| `in_progress` | `running` |
| `needs_input` | `blocked` |
| `paused` | `idle` |
| `pending` | `idle` |
| `processing` | `running` |
| `queued` | `idle` |
| `sleeping` | `idle` |
| `succeeded` | `done` |
| `success` | `done` |
| `waiting` | `idle` |
| `working` | `running` |

## A complete document

```json
{
  "schema": "agentfs/v1",
  "status": "running",
  "agent": "researcher",
  "task": "Retrieve and rank sources",
  "step": 3,
  "steps_total": 8,
  "model": "claude-opus-5",
  "run_id": "eval-2026-04-08-a",
  "heartbeat_seconds": 30,
  "started_at": "2026-04-08T12:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-04-08T13:00:00Z",
  "labels": {
    "queue": "batch"
  }
}
```

## Writing it

Write the document atomically: to a temporary file in the same directory, flushed, then renamed over the target. A reader opens the file at moments the writer does not choose, and a writer that truncates the target and streams into it hands that reader bytes that are not JSON. agentfs holds the last complete reading rather than flickering, and reports the torn read — but the fix belongs to the writer.

Reference writers to vendor are in [contrib](../../contrib): one file each for Python and TypeScript, with no dependencies.
